text:
incident-bot: ALERT: prod-serving-gpu pool - cudaOOM observed on node gpu-14 at 21:07 UTC. headroom reported ~600MB available by headroom metric. auto-escalation to #incidents triggered.

michael: oncall here, ACK. can someone grab the node logs and nvidia-smi? curious how OOM happened with headroom.

sara: grabbing logs now. running: `ssh ubuntu@gpu-14 'sudo journalctl -u redwood-serving -n 200'` and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.total --format=csv`

sara: nvidia-smi output: 
```
memory.used [MiB], memory.total [MiB]
15014 MiB, 16130 MiB
```

sara: container restarted automatically by k8s: crashloop backoff. journalctl shows CUDA out of memory at allocation of 1.2GB inside allocator. posting allocator debug slice.

sara: allocator debug snippet: 
```
[2026-03-15T21:06:52Z] runtime::gpu::alloc() -> trying reserve 128MB from sparepool
[2026-03-15T21:06:52Z] runtime::gpu::reserve() -> reserved blocks: 3, free_blocks: 1, fragmentation_ratio: 0.82
[2026-03-15T21:06:52Z] runtime::gpu::alloc() -> cannot find contiguous chunk, falling back to deviceAlloc -> cudaErrorMemoryAllocation
```

jordan: interesting — fragmentation_ratio high, sparepool entries low. headroom metric we use is total_free - but doesn't account for contiguous-run availability. sounds like large contiguous allocation needed for KV cache prefetch or big batch.

michael: any recent changes to reserve slab sizes or KV prefetch config in the last deploy? deploy-bot reported a canary earlier today.

deploy-bot: Noted: deploy 2026-03-15T19:55 — runtime: bump kv_prefetch_workers from 5 -> 12 in canary.

ops-runner: that change would increase in-memory KV prefetch concurrency and could increase fragmentation if allocations are interleaved.

alice-cs: customer-impact note: some customers reported increase in 503s around 21:06 - 21:09 UTC, about ~3m window. CS flagged three accounts with higher error rates, started inbound tickets.

michael: mitigation plan immediate: 1) cordon node gpu-14 2) drain non-critical pods 3) restart serving pod(s) with reduced kv_prefetch_workers to avoid large contiguous allocations 4) enable emergency force-evict of sparepool chunks (if available) 5) monitor. Sara, can you run cordon + drain now?

sara: doing: `kubectl cordon gpu-14 && kubectl drain gpu-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — starting drain now.

sara: also temp-patching config locally and restarting the crashlooping pod with env OVERRIDE_KV_PREFETCH=3 to validate recovery without redeploy.

sara: restart command log: 
```
kubectl set env deploy/serving-worker OVERRIDE_KV_PREFETCH=3 -n prod --record
kubectl rollout restart deploy/serving-worker -n prod --field-selector spec.nodeName=gpu-14
```

sara: pod restarted, container came up cleanly. memory now: 
```
memory.used 10320 MiB, memory.total 16130 MiB
```

jordan: good sign. that points to allocation pattern rather than driver leak. need to confirm if reserve slabs are being reserved but not defragmented on prefetch failure.

michael: while drain completes, let's also surface this to eng-runtime and eng-infra for follow-up. create a ticket and triage owner. I'll assign to @jordan and @sara.

ops-runner: filing ticket: RD-INC-2026-317 (temporary id) — summary: "CUDA OOM on gpu-14 despite headroom: fragmentation & kv_prefetch concurrency". linking logs and nvidia-smi, allocator debug, deploy change.

alice-cs: customer update draft: "We experienced a brief outage affecting some requests between 21:06-21:09 UTC due to an internal GPU memory failure. We've mitigated the issue by restarting affected pods and applying a temporary configuration to reduce memory fragmentation. We'll follow up with a root cause analysis and timeline. Apologize for the disruption." ok to send?

michael: send after we confirm node stable for 15m. Sara, how's drain progress?

sara: drain finished. node gpu-14 cordoned and drained. no more crashloops. monitoring shows healthy request latencies on remaining pool nodes — small traffic bump as k8s rescheduled.

incident-bot: NOTE: automatic incident severity assigned P2 due to customer error spikes and partial service degradation.

jordan: next steps for post-incident: 1) collect heap snapshots and VM maps from affected timeframe (we have allocator dump but need live defrag traces) 2) add instrumentation to headroom metric to include contiguous-chunk availability 3) assess reverting kv_prefetch_workers bump or making it adaptive by batch size 4) run synthetic stress test with high prefetch concurrency to reproduce fragmentation 5) coordinate with infra about potential NVIDIA driver/OS-level allocation behavior that affects contiguous allocations.

michael: agree. also consider short-term policy: set a hard upper bound on per-pod contiguous alloc request (fallback to smaller chunk allocations) and improved graceful fallback path — avoid immediate crash on deviceAlloc failure.

alice-cs: I've sent the customer note and included a proactive offer to review impacted request logs. customers responded with thanks and asked for ETA on RCA.

ops-runner: adding owners on the ticket: eng-runtime (jordan), eng-infra (sara), devex (michael) for monitoring/dashboard changes. SLA follow-up in the ticket.

sara: oncall handoff — I'm going off-shift in ~20m. michael, are you handing off to jordan?

michael: yes. jordan will be primary for the remainder. I'll stay reachable. jordan, take it.

jordan: taking it. I'll run the stress reproducer tonight against a staging fleet with kv_prefetch_workers=12 and an allocation pattern that forces big contiguous requests.

incident-bot: ACTION: created incident checklist RD-INC-2026-317/checklist, assigned owners.

michael: quick retrospective note in thread for postmortem: time to detect and auto-roll back risky config can be improved. current canary window didn't catch fragmentation pattern. consider adding a fragmentation regression test to canary suite.

alice-cs: customers updated; two accounts requested incident timeline once RCA is ready. I'll keep them posted.

jordan: once we have reproducer, I'll propose a mitigation: allocator should try to coalesce free blocks lazily and, if contiguous chunk not found, try smaller chunk allocations instead of immediate OOM. we'll also evaluate increasing sparepool slab fragmentation tolerance.

michael: thanks team. leaving the channel to jordan. pls ensure the postmortem covers: root cause hypothesis, why headroom metric missed contiguous availability, deploy/config change correlation, immediate mitigations, and long-term fixes.

jordan: will do. Closing this operational thread — moving discussion to RD-INC-2026-317 ticket and #eng-runtime for technical deep dive. :wave:
